newsitem.title: NORWAY: Belo, Ramos-Hortas share Nobel Peace Prize.
newsitem.headline: Belo, Ramos-Hortas share Nobel Peace Prize.

text.p: Bishop Carlos Belo and Jose Ramos-Horta were jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize for their efforts to bring peace in the former Portuguese territory of East Timor, the Norwegian Nobel Committee said on Friday.
They shared the prize "for their work toward a just and peaceful solution to the conflict in East Timor," Committee Chairman Francis Sejersted said.

"Belo...has been the foremost representative of the people of East Timor. At the risk of his own life, he has tried to protect his people from infringements by those in power," the committee said in a statement.
Belo, East Timor's outspoken and often fiery Roman Catholic bishop, is long used to walking a tightrope between his flock and the Indonesian government which controls the territory.
He was holding a Mass at a school in the territory's capital of Dili on Friday when the prestigious award was announced.
The committee said Ramos-Horta "has been the leading international spokesman for East Timor's cause since 1975 when Indonesia seized control of East Timor".
In Lisbon, Ramos-Horta, a spokesman for the East Timor resistance movement, said he was happy but also sad at the award because his jailed leader Xanana Gusmao should have won.
"I receive the news with pleasure and with sadness," Ramos-Horta said in a radio interview.
Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio welcomed the award saying it recognised the untiring work the two men had carried out "in the service of human rights and peace in the territory".
"I am very pleased by the news. It is a wonderful surprise," Sampaio told reporters.
